input.subject: 18 Juniper Fold – damp inspection (ref NBL-4821 / R/026)
input.body:
Dear Iris,

Thank you for your update and for letting us know about the stain.

Inspection: yes, the inspection is still going ahead. The surveyor from Brindle Survey & Drying had a vehicle breakdown and couldn't attend today. He has offered Friday 7 March after 13:00 instead. You told us earlier that weekday afternoons after 13:00 suit you. Could you reply to confirm you can give access that afternoon? Once you do, we'll confirm the slot with him. This is still a non-intrusive inspection only.

Socket under the window: thank you for checking. Until it has been inspected, please keep the area dry and avoid using that socket if you can. If you notice any dampness on the socket, heat, a burning smell, sparks or a tripped breaker, stop using it, switch it off at the fuse box if it's safe to do so, and call us straight away.

The email you received in error: thank you for handling this so carefully. For now, please keep not forwarding, sharing or using it. Our privacy team is reviewing it and will contact you directly with clear instructions on whether to delete it. Please don't do anything else with it until you hear from them.

We'll follow up by tomorrow morning if we haven't heard from you.

Kind regards,
Donna
Northbridge Lettings – Maintenance

I kept the damp inspection moving myself: I told the tenant the inspection is still going ahead, gave her precautions for the socket and asked her to confirm access on 7 March. I asked the contractor to hold that slot provisionally, keeping the work non-intrusive as approved, and set a follow-up for tomorrow morning.
result.situation: Damp staining below the kitchen window at 18 Juniper Fold. The owner approved only a non-intrusive inspection fee (event 011). The inspection was booked for 6 March with Owen Pike of Brindle Survey & Drying, but he missed it because of a vehicle breakdown and offered 7 March after 13:00 instead (event 019). Separately, on 5 March the appointment confirmation sent to tenant Iris Bell also contained another tenant's name, address, arrears amount and payment arrangement (event 013). Elena Frost, the privacy lead, is gathering facts (events 017–018) but no decision is recorded. On 6 March Iris asked whether the inspection is still happening and whether she should keep that email, and said the stain is darker. The stain is near a socket, but she reports no dripping and no electrical symptoms (event 020).

escalation.reason: A personal data breach (another tenant's arrears data sent to Iris Bell) has no recorded assessment or notification decision, and the recipient is asking what to do with the email.
escalation.handover_summary: The appointment email on 5 March at 11:22 included another tenant's name, address, arrears and payment arrangement. It went only to Iris, with no attachment. She has not forwarded it and still has it in her inbox. The affected tenant has not been contacted. No ICO or notification decision is recorded. If the agency became aware at about 11:29 on 5 March, the 72-hour window would end at about 11:29 on 8 March. I told Iris to keep not sharing it and to wait for the privacy team's instructions.
escalation.recommendation: Today, Elena Frost should record the risk assessment and the ICO decision, decide whether to tell the affected tenant, and send Iris written deletion instructions once the agency's copy is preserved. Someone should also correct the contractor contact on the ticket to Owen Pike, Brindle Survey & Drying.

judgement.why_this_decision: The breach (events 013–018) is a legal and privacy matter that needs agency judgement. There is a possible ICO deadline and no decision after about 29 hours, so it needed a high-priority human escalation. Whether Iris keeps or deletes the email is for the privacy lead, so I only repeated the existing instruction not to share it (event 015). The maintenance side is routine: the owner approved the inspection (event 011), the contractor offered a new slot (event 019), and the tenant's stated availability (event 004) fits it. So I asked her to confirm, asked the contractor to hold the slot, and placed a hold. The darkening stain near the socket, with no symptoms, does not count as an emergency. I gave precautions and asked the contractor to flag whether an electrician is needed.

alternatives_considered.option: Tell Iris to delete the email
alternatives_considered.why_not: The privacy lead asked for the message to be preserved and has made no decision. Telling her to delete it could get ahead of the agency's assessment.

alternatives_considered.option: Confirm 7 March directly with the contractor
alternatives_considered.why_not: The tenant hasn't confirmed that specific date, and the outbound guard blocked it as unconfirmed.

alternatives_considered.option: Treat the darkening stain near the socket as an electrical emergency
alternatives_considered.why_not: There is no dripping, heat, sparking or tripping (events 009, 020). Precautions and escalation triggers are proportionate.

alternatives_considered.option: Create a CRM approval record by sending the landlord a new approval request
alternatives_considered.why_not: He has already approved by email. Asking again would duplicate the request and confuse him. I left the stage gap noted instead.
